annotations.title: Get Distress Watch (Daily Delisting and Bankruptcy Report)

description: One day's record of listing distress at US-listed companies, in six sections: upcomingSuspensions (exchange trading suspensions dated in the next five trading sessions), delistingActions (Staff delisting determinations, hearing requests and stated intents to request one, stays, Hearings Panel exceptions and denials, second compliance periods and suspension notices filed that day, read from 8-K and 6-K filings, company press releases and NYSE Regulation releases), newDeficiencies (new deficiency notices grouped by listing standard, each row keeping the rule cited, plus names new to the Nasdaq non-compliant list), bankruptcies (8-K Item 1.03 filings and tagged bankruptcy events; emergences and funds excluded), complianceRegained, and recentlyRemoved (Form 25 under Exchange Act Rule 12d2-2(b), the exchange striking the security; mergers and redemptions excluded). Events are dated after window.from (the previous trading date) up to and including date. Each row has ticker, companyName, kind, eventDate, statedDeadline with deadlineBasis, standards, rule, exchange, the source (form, dashed accession, link), lastClose with lastCloseAsOf, and detail (hearingDate, suspensionDate, bankruptcy stage, Form 25 effectiveOn). statedDeadline is set only when the exchange or an accepted compliance plan states the date; Signal8 estimates are never included. note reads "Reverse split within the prior 12 months ... so no cure period" only when a recorded reverse split executed within 365 days before a Nasdaq bid-price matter, with priorReverseSplit giving its date and ratio. A null field means not measured: it never means no, zero or none. An empty section is a normal result. Facts of record, not advice.

date.description: ET report date, YYYY-MM-DD (default today ET). Not in the future, within the last 400 days.
